chainFacts.says: Classic SPL mint, 6 decimals, supply 0 on Solana; readable by the /fungible reader, which would show an empty leg.
One address, 6ViaRWzv7p56RfP1A9Hxy2ctu9kfE3XL43SxWuq3E4cE, is mint and freeze authority; no extensions. Who holds the key is not in the sources.
The older catalogue also found the Solana supply at 0 on 16 September 2026, while Ondo's page showed $330.7M TVL; it says instant mint and redeem run on Ethereum only.

outside.says: Instant atomic USDC redemption and a standard route with different cutoffs and minimums ($5,000 and $50,000), subject to the product's rules; no redemption was tested.

The product page describes a fee waiver or cap subject to terms (the older catalogue: 0.15% management fee, waived until July 2026); class valuation, distribution rules and gates need the fund documents.
The older catalogue says OUSG is offered under Reg D Rule 506(c) as a 3(c)(7) fund; that is an exemption from registration, not a registration.
rOUSG is a rebasing variant; Polygon and XRP Ledger tokens represent the same exposure, with bridge design and controls unverified.

verdict.summary: The Solana mint is classic SPL and readable, but empty. The fund-of-funds shape fits v3 well: BUIDL's registrar can make a register entry about the BUIDL mint for the OUSG vehicle. That BUIDL mint is Token-2022, though, and nothing can stop a reader from adding the two funds' backing together. The holder's legal form (an LP or fund interest) has no claim kind, and which record prevails is a proposal. Apart from Ondo itself, no party publishes anything in its own name, and the custodian and administrator are named only in the older catalogue.
